The GB notification service prototype (GOV.UK Prototype Kit, Nunjucks views, one Express router) at ~/git/defra/defra-design/GB-notification-service, commit c2078fb (the checkout's HEAD is c2078fb, so files can be read in place; use git show c2078fb:<path> if it has moved). The previous extract was taken at 04a073b; 70 commits since then add a gross weight page, a delete-document page, an amend confirmation page, a postcode find-address journey, germinal templates, per-commodity identification fields, a generated full commodity list and dashboard filter and status changes, and grow app/routes.js from 13,114 to 15,341 lines. Design Release 2.1 is not a separate app: app/lib/design-release-2.1-version.js (42 lines) calls app/lib/version-mount.js (365 lines), which copies every route in app/routes.js under /design-release-2.1, keeps a separate session nest (_designRelease21, flag _isDesignRelease21Version), prefixes journey paths in redirects and render data, sets service-navigation hrefs, and renders app/views/design-release-2.1/<view>.html where one exists, otherwise the root view. DR2.1 also sets isDesignRelease2Version. Handlers branch on isDesignRelease21SessionData, hasJourneyUpdates (true for DR2.1, Testing 3 and Testing 4), isDesignRelease21OnlySessionData (DR2.1 without the Testing flags) and isRound2TestingSessionData (Testing 3 and 4 only, so branches under it do not apply to DR2.1). app/routes.js: lines 1-96 are requires and constants, lines 97-12688 are about 600 helper functions (session, validation, view models, render functions), lines 12689-15139 are about 120 route handlers including the generated consignment-address section routes, lines 15140-15331 are the sign-in redirect and the postcode find-address spike (mountFindAddress, mounted for the address book and each selectable consignment section), and lines 15332-15341 mount the versions. Views in scope: the 39 DR2.1 overrides in app/views/design-release-2.1/ (about 5,000 lines), the 19 DR2.1 partials in app/views/partials/design-release-2.1/ (about 1,100 lines), the root views DR2.1 falls back on (index, address-book, address-book-add, address-book-add-usage, address-book-lookup, address-book-view, find-address, find-address-select, postcode-lookup; about 1,300 lines), the root partials the DR2.1 pages include or routes.js renders (notification-status, region-of-origin-code-input, arrival-date-picker, cph-number-input, permanent-address-new-address-fields, the four reason-for-import selects, the transporter fields and banner, address-book-manual-address-fields), and layouts/main.html and layouts/journey.html (which now includes partials/design-release-2.1/cancel-amend-modal.html). app/data/ holds 35 list files (about 4,200 lines) plus app/data/generated/. Cut into 17 parts by what a user sees, keeping the previous extract's 16 themes and numbering so its claims fall to the same part: the shell and journey control, then the journey in page order (start, consignment and gross weight, reason, identification, arrival and transit, transporter, roles and addresses, CPH and permanent address, documents, review and submit), then notification hub with amend and copy, dashboard, templates, the address book in two parts, and a new part 17 for the postcode find-address pages. routes.js is too big for one agent, so each part reads the routes.js line ranges that hold its pages' helpers, render functions and handlers; the ranges tile lines 1-15341 with no gaps or overlaps, and a view, partial or data file shared by two parts is read by both but claimed only for the pages the part names. Left out by scope: app/views/intro/ and intro/routes.js; app/views/testing/, testing3/, testing4/ and their partials folders, and app/lib/testing-version.js, testing3-version.js and testing4-version.js (the design-release-2 folders no longer exist at this commit); and the root journey views DR2.1 overrides, including the unused root review-summary-card, review-summary-row, animal-identification-saved-animals and dashboard-date-range-input partials. Also left out: app/assets/ (client-side JavaScript, Sass and assets/data/common-names-live.json, not named by the scope; the rendered traces source covers client behaviour); app/data/generated/commodities-live.json (8,259 lines of generated catalogue, read through commodities.js and described by generated/README.md; the commodity catalogue waits on MDM and app/data is no evidence for data) and app/data/generated/postcode-addresses/ (one generated Companies House fixture per postcode district); and three files nothing in scope reads (app/data/package-types.js, app/data/place-of-origin-addresses.js, used only by intro/routes.js, and app/views/testing*/cancel-amend-notification.html, which only Testing 3 and 4 render).

claims.statement: Design release 2.1 is served under the base path /design-release-2.1.

Every route of the root router is copied under /design-release-2.1 (each method of each route, with the same handlers), so DR2.1 has the same pages and handlers as the root journey rather than its own route table.
Only route layers are copied into the version router: router-level middleware and the catch-all _all method are not copied.
claims.note: mechanism: copies the root router's route table into the version router.

claims.statement: The versions are mounted in the order Testing 4, Testing 3, Testing and then Design release 2.1; the longer /testing paths go before /testing so they are not taken as /testing paths. No separate design release 2 version is mounted.
claims.quote:
// Mount the longer /testing* paths before /testing so Express does not treat them as that route
mountTesting4Version(govukPrototypeKit, router)
mountTesting3Version(govukPrototypeKit, router)
mountTestingVersion(govukPrototypeKit, router)
mountDesignRelease21Version(govukPrototypeKit, router)

claims.statement: Under /design-release-2.1 the session data a page sees is a separate nest stored under the session key _designRelease21, so DR2.1 notifications, drafts and answers are kept apart from the root journey and the other versions.
Inside the DR2.1 session nest the flag _isDesignRelease21Version is set to true on every request, which handlers use to tell they are running as DR2.1.

Two session keys are shared across all versions rather than kept in the DR2.1 nest: the addresses added to the address book (addressBookAddedAddresses) and the submitted notifications (submittedNotifications). Reading or writing them in DR2.1 reads or writes the shared value.

When a DR2.1 request carries a form or query field (not starting with an underscore, not the session key and not a shared key) whose name also exists in the shared session outside the DR2.1 nest, the nest takes the outer session's value for that key before the handler runs.
claims.note: mechanism: copies outer session values into the version nest. The posted value itself is applied later by the prototype kit. Recorded as observed, not interpreted further.

claims.statement: Before a DR2.1 response redirects or ends, the session is restored so the DR2.1 nest is saved back under _designRelease21 in the full session.
claims.note: mechanism: saves the version session nest.

claims.statement: Every DR2.1 page is given the requested URL, query string included, as currentPath.

In DR2.1, a redirect to a journey path is prefixed with /design-release-2.1 (for example a redirect to /notification-hub goes to /design-release-2.1/notification-hub), and a redirect to / goes to /design-release-2.1.

A link or redirect to / with a query string (/?...) becomes /design-release-2.1?... in DR2.1, and a journey path keeps its query string and fragment after the prefix; whether a path is a journey path is decided on the path without its query string or fragment.

In DR2.1, every string in the data passed to a page render that is a journey path is prefixed with /design-release-2.1, so links, form actions and back links built by handlers stay inside the version.
claims.note: mechanism: rewrites every string in a page's render data, nested objects and arrays and the data object included.

claims.statement: The journey path prefixes that are kept inside the version are: /create-notification, /notification-type, /origin-of-the-import, /what-are-you-importing, /reason-for-import, /consignment-details, /consignment-gross-weight, /animal-identification-details, /additional-animal-details, /arrival-details, /transit-countries, /transporter, /upload-documents, /roles-and-addresses, /place-of-origin, /consignor-or-exporter, /consignee, /importer, /place-of-destination, /cph-number, /permanent-address, /contact-address-for-consignment, /review-notification, /declaration, /notification-submitted, /notification-hub, /notifications, /dashboard, /live-animals, /germinal-products, /templates, /actions, /changes, /inspection and /prototype/reason-for-import (each path itself or anything below it).
Paths that are not journey paths are left unprefixed: external or protocol-relative links, links not starting with /, fragment links starting with #, and any path not in the journey prefix list.

The address book (/address-book and anything below it), static assets (/public/, /plugin-assets/), the prototype kit management pages (/manage-prototype) and the service index (/index) are shared paths that are never prefixed with the version base path.

return urlPath === '/address-book' ||

    urlPath.startsWith('/public/') ||

claims.statement: The origin page normally shows a single "Save and continue" button, with no save-and-return-to-overview button and no cancel link: it turns both off and the shared actions default the button text.
Saving the origin page with the "return to overview" or "return to review" action skips validation, saves the draft and goes to the notification hub or the review page.

A valid origin page continues to /what-are-you-importing, or back to the notification hub when opened from the hub, to the review page when opened from review, or to the template review when editing a template.
When the origin or commodity page is opened from the notification hub, the form carries from=hub so that saving returns to the hub.
Origin details count as complete only when a country is chosen and the region question is answered, and, when the answer is Yes, a region of origin code suffix is held.
The commodity page can be opened without origin details: its guard against missing origin never redirects.
GET /what-are-you-importing makes sure the notification has a design-release reference and clears any leftover search text before showing the page.
The commodity page has the caption "About the consignment" and the heading "What are you importing?", which is also its page name.

The commodity page shows inset text: "You must submit a separate notification for every single health certificate. You must also submit a notification for goods that do not need an health certificate."

claims.note: The source says "an health certificate". The earlier ITAHC wording is commented out at lines 42-45.

claims.statement: The commodity page's back link goes to /origin-of-the-import, or to the notification hub when opened from the hub, or to the template review when editing a template from review.
The commodity search field is labelled "Search for a commodity".

claims.statement: The commodity search is a search box with a search button ("Search", visually hidden text), a results list labelled "Commodity search results" and a polite live region for status messages.

claims.statement: The commodity page shows the user's selections in a panel with a heading and a "Clear all" button that is hidden until something is selected.
claims.note: The heading element is empty in the view; its text is set client-side. "Clear all" is the button text.

claims.statement: The commodity page submits its selections in hidden fields: a commodity id, a commodity code, the selected species and the full list of selections.

claims.statement: How the commodity and country searches behave in the browser (matching, result layout, picking species, the selection panel heading, removing a single selection) is not defined in the server code or views this source scopes in.
claims.note: app/assets/ is out of scope; the traces source covers client behaviour.

claims.statement: In DR2.1 the commodity search lists only germinal-product commodities when the notification type is germinal products, and only live-animal commodities when it is live animals.

In DR2.1, for live animals the commodity search offers the generated live-animal list plus four extra commodities (Gamebirds: day-old chicks, Gamebirds: adult birds, Poultry: day-old chicks, Poultry: adult birds), all sorted by name.
claims.note: hasJourneyUpdates is true whenever the DR2.1 flag is set.

claims.statement: For plants for planting, potatoes, wood products, or no type, the DR2.1 commodity search has nothing to offer, so a user on those types cannot select a commodity and cannot pass the commodity page's validation.
The commodity page gives the search a list of common English animal names (/public/data/common-names-live.json) only for live animals in DR2.1; for germinal products or any other type it gives none.

Commodity search results are sorted alphabetically by commodity name, and each commodity's species are sorted by "common name (Latin name)", or by "commodity name (Latin name)" when a species has no common name.
claims.note: Sorting ignores case and accents (sensitivity: 'base').

claims.statement: Each commodity search entry offers the commodity's id, name, code and species, and each species its id, Latin name and (where it has one) common name.
claims.quote:
id: commodity.id,
      name: commodity.name,
      code: commodity.code,

claims.statement: Each commodity search entry also carries the commodity's search terms and its full tariff codes where it has them, and each species its search terms, so search can match other names and codes beyond the name, Latin name and main code.
The commodity page opens with the notification's existing selections already chosen, filtered to those that match the current notification type.

The commodity page's pre-chosen selections can include whole commodities as well as species: saved selections of either kind are restored, and with none saved it falls back to the saved species, then to the saved main commodity.

The commodity page has a "Help with commodity codes" details component explaining: "Commodity codes are internationally recognised reference numbers." and "A commodity code describes a specific product when importing or exporting goods."
claims.note: Paragraph quotes: "Commodity codes are internationally recognised reference numbers." and "A commodity code describes a specific product when importing or exporting goods."

claims.statement: The commodity page uses the default journey buttons: "Save and continue", a secondary "Save and return to overview" button and a "Cancel and return to overview" link to the notification hub, because it sets no options of its own.
claims.note: When creating a template, the shared actions read "Save and return to template" and "Cancel and return to template" instead.

claims.statement: If nothing is selected, the commodity page shows the error "Select a commodity", inline and in the summary, linking to the commodity search box.

The commodity page passes validation with either selected species or a list of selections, so a whole commodity chosen with no species passes; that commodity is then kept in the saved list of selections, while the saved species list stays empty.
claims.note: mechanism: works on selectedSpecies and commoditySelections in the session. Origin-of-the-import and later pages that read only species (hasCommoditySelection) would treat such a notification as having no commodity.

claims.statement: A notification counts as having a commodity selection only when at least one species is selected.
Pages after the commodity page can be opened without a commodity selection: the guard against a missing commodity never redirects.
Submitted species and selections that do not belong to the notification's type are dropped before saving (for example, a germinal-product species on a live-animals notification).
A commodity belongs to germinal products if it is flagged as a germinal product; every other commodity belongs to live animals; for any other notification type, all commodities match.
Species ids that match no known species are dropped when the selection is saved.
Selected species may be submitted as a list, a JSON array, a single JSON string or a comma-separated string.
claims.note: mechanism: parses the selectedSpecies form value. An object of values is also accepted.

claims.statement: The saved selection records each selected species with its commodity id, commodity code and species id.
claims.quote:
type: 'species',

        commodityCode: match.commodity.code,

claims.statement: The notification's main commodity (id, code and name) is the commodity of the first selected species; with no species it is cleared.
When every selected species is under commodity code 01061900 (cat, dog, ferret or other live mammals), any unweaned animals answer is cleared.

Saving the commodity page with the "return to overview" or "return to review" action skips validation, saves any valid species selection, saves the draft and goes to the notification hub or review page.

After a valid commodity selection, the user goes on to /reason-for-import, or back to the hub, review or template review as the entry point dictates; when creating a template, the user goes to the notification hub.
Removing a species from the selection also removes its number of animals, number of packages, germinal packages, net weight and package type.
Removing a commodity removes all of its selected species, along with each species' number of animals, number of packages, germinal packages, net weight and package type.
claims.note: The routes that call these removals are in other parts.

A selected species is titled "code (common name - Latin name)", using the commodity name when the species has no common name, for example "0102 (Domestic cattle - Bos taurus)".

A species' label in a list of selected species is its Latin name, or its common name when it has no Latin name; in DR2.1, when the page asks for the updated label, it leads with the common name as "common name (Latin name)", unless the common name only repeats the commodity name or the Latin name.

claims.statement: Copy as new and amend with ?submitted=<id> use that submitted notification's saved snapshot; if no submitted notification has that id, the user is sent back to the dashboard.

Copy as new and amend with ?reference=<reference> use that dashboard notification's saved snapshot, or build one from its dashboard details when it has none; if the reference is not found, the user is sent back to the dashboard.
Copy as new and amend with neither ?submitted nor ?reference use the notification currently in the session.
'Back to the dashboard' from these routes means the design release's own dashboard path (such as /design-release-2.1), or / when there is none.

Copy as new starts a fresh notification: it clears the journey, keeping only the user's address book additions, drafts, submitted notifications, deleted references, saved and deleted templates and the version flags.
Copy as new carries over the import details: country of origin, whether a region of origin is required, the region of origin code and its suffix, and the internal reference.
Copy as new carries over what is being imported: the selected species, commodity selections, commodity id, code and name, and the notification type.

Copy as new carries over the main reason for import and its follow-ups: import reason, internal market purpose, transhipment destination country, transit exit border control post, transit destination country, temporary admission exit date and temporary admission port of exit.
Copy as new carries over the additional animal details: certification purpose, unweaned animals and storage temperature.

Copy as new carries over the roles and addresses: place of origin, consignor, consignee, importer and place of destination addresses (with their ids), the CPH number, and the permanent address details (address, id, same-as-destination answer, summary and animals).

Copy as new does not carry over the shipment-specific details: the number of animals, packages and net weight, animal identifiers, port of entry, arrival date, transport, transit countries, transporter, uploaded documents or the contact address. The user enters these again.
claims.note: Inferred from what the carried-over list leaves out, compared with the fields a snapshot holds (for example dashboard-notification-snapshots.js:62-97 and 159-172).

claims.statement: Only fields that have a value in the source are copied; each copied value is a deep copy, so changing the new notification does not change the original.

When copying, an older certification purpose is mapped to a current option: 'Breeding' and 'Breeding and/or production' become 'Further keeping', 'Slaughter' stays 'Slaughter', and any other value not in the current options becomes 'Further keeping'.
If the copied notification has no notification type, it is worked out from the copied answers.
The copy gets a new notification reference and the status 'Draft', with no errors.
The copy is saved as a draft straight away, before the user changes anything.
After copying, the user is taken to the notification hub.
POST /notifications/amend starts the amendment.
Starting an amendment works only in a session with the Design Release 2.1 flag, otherwise it redirects to /. When the notification cannot be found, the user is sent back to the dashboard.

Amend loads the whole saved notification into the session, replacing the current journey answers but keeping the drafts, submitted notifications, deleted references, address book additions and version flags.
claims.note: Unlike resetNotificationJourneySession, this list does not keep savedTemplates or deletedTemplateIds, so loading a snapshot for amend may drop saved templates unless the snapshot carries them.

claims.statement: An amended notification keeps its original reference: the snapshot's reference, else the ?reference value, else a newly generated one.
While amending, the notification's status is 'Amend'.
Amend records which notification is being amended, by submitted id and by reference, so that submitting replaces it and cancelling returns to it.
Amend keeps a copy of the notification as it was before the amendment, for change detection, and clears any errors.
After choosing to amend, the user is taken to the review page of the notification.
A notification counts as changed during an amendment when its answers differ from the copy taken when the amendment started; with no copy taken it never counts as changed.

Change detection ignores everything that is not a notification answer: errors, messages, the commodity search box, the status, the amend bookkeeping, version flags, drafts, submitted notifications, saved templates, deleted references and address book additions.
What the page does with the amend change check (for example, whether submitting an unchanged amendment is blocked) is not in this slice.

claims.statement: The filter has a select labelled "Type", named type, whose first option is "Select one" with an empty value.

On the other tabs the Type filter offers only the address types that belong to that tab's category, drawn from the address-type list (which has no divider entry).

So the Origin and Consignor tab's Type filter offers "Place of Origin" and "Consignor"; the Destination, Consignee and Importer tab offers "Consignee", "Importer" and "Place of Destination"; the Branch tab offers "Branch Address". The category's other types (consignor-or-exporter, exporter, contact, packer) have no filter option.

claims.statement: Under Design Release 2 and 2.1 the list is split into four category tabs, in this order: "Origin and Consignor", "Destination, Consignee and Importer", "Transporter" and "Branch".
Each tab panel has its own heading: "Origin and Consignor addresses", "Destination, Consignee and Importer addresses", "Transporter addresses" or "Branch addresses".

The Origin and Consignor category holds the place-of-origin, consignor, consignor-or-exporter and exporter types; Destination, Consignee and Importer holds consignee, importer, place-of-destination, contact and packer; Transporter holds transporter; Branch holds branch-address.
The selected tab comes from the category query parameter; when it is missing or unknown the Origin and Consignor tab is shown.
The older category values origin-and-sender and destination-and-receiver are accepted as aliases of origin-and-consignor and destination-consignee-importer.
An address appears on every tab whose category holds any of its types, so an address with several types can appear on more than one tab.
Each tab link goes to page 1 of that category, keeps the current search and drops the type filter.
Above the table, a results line reads "Showing <start>-<end> of <total>", or "Showing 0 of 0" when nothing matches.
On every tab except Transporter the table's columns are Name, Type, Address and Country, followed by an action column with the visually hidden header "Action".
On the Transporter tab the table's columns are Name, Address, Approval number and Type, followed by the action column.
In the Name column a name of more than one word is shown on two lines: the first word, then the rest.
claims.note: mechanism: splits an address's name into two display lines.

claims.statement: In the Address column each address line is shown on its own line, ending in a comma except the last.
In the Type column an address with several types shows their labels joined by a comma and space.

The list shows type labels "Place of origin", "Consignor" (for consignor, consignor-or-exporter and exporter), "Consignee", "Importer", "Place of destination", "Transporter", "Branch", "Contact address" and "Packer"; these differ in case and wording from the filter options ("Place of Origin", "Branch Address").
A transporter's Type is its own type, Commercial or Private, defaulting to Commercial; its Country is taken as the last comma-separated part of its address.
claims.note: mechanism: derives a transporter's country from the last part of its free-text address.

claims.statement: Each row ends with a "View" link to that address's view page.
The list shows 8 addresses per page.
When there is more than one page, pagination shows a numbered link to every page with the current one marked, plus "Previous" and "Next" links where they apply.
Pagination links keep the category, search and type filter and add page only for pages after the first.
A page number below 1 or not a number shows page 1, and one beyond the last page shows the last page.
When no address matches, the list shows an empty table and "Showing 0 of 0", with no empty-state message or prompt to add an address.
claims.note: No empty-state copy exists in the template; inferred from the table rendering zero rows.

claims.statement: The list shows addresses the user added this session first, then the seeded addresses less any deleted this session, each with any edits made this session applied.
Additions, edits and deletions in the address book are held in the user's prototype session only, not saved anywhere else.
claims.note: Prototype persistence; the real service is expected to persist to the address-book service. Inferred from every write going to req.session.data.

claims.statement: The address view page is served at GET /address-book/:addressId.
The view page can show any address the service knows by id, searching the address book first and then consignment addresses, contact addresses and transporters.
If no address has that id, the view page redirects to its back link: the return path, or the address book list.
The view page has a "Back" link to the return query path when one is given, otherwise to the address book list.

A return path is honoured only when it starts with a single /; anything else falls back to the default, and an unversioned /address-book path is rewritten to the Design Release's own address book path.
The view page's heading is the address's name.
The view page's summary list always shows the rows "Name or organisation name", "Address line 1", "Town or city", "Postcode or Zip code", "Country", "Email address" and "Phone number".
The view page shows "Address line 2 (optional)" after Address line 1 and "County (optional)" after Town or city only when they have a value.
The view page's row values come from the address's stored details or, failing those, are split from its address lines into the manual fields.
claims.note: mechanism: reshapes stored address lines into the nine manual fields for display.

claims.statement: When the address is in the address book, the view page shows a secondary "Edit" button and a warning "Delete" button; an address found only elsewhere (a consignment, contact or transporter address) shows neither.
The Edit button links to <address book>/<id>/edit and the Delete button to <address book>/<id>/delete, each carrying the view page's return path when it is not the list itself.
The edit page is served at GET /address-book/:addressId/edit; if the id is not in the address book it redirects to the return path or the list.

The edit page's "Back" link goes to the return path when given, otherwise to the address's view page.

claims.statement: The delete page is served at GET /address-book/:addressId/delete; if the id is not in the address book it redirects to the return path or the list.

claims.statement: The delete page has a warning button "Yes, delete" that posts to <address book>/<id>/delete, carrying the return path when it is not the list.
The delete page has a "No, cancel" link and a "Back" link, both to the address's view page with the return path carried on.
Confirming the delete removes the address from the address book: an address added this session is removed outright, and a seeded address is recorded as deleted and any edit to it discarded.
After a delete the list shows a success banner reading "<Name> address deleted", with the name's first letter capitalised and the rest lower-cased, or "Address deleted" when the name is blank.
claims.note: The banner text ends with a full stop: "address deleted." and "Address deleted.".

claims.statement: After a delete the user goes to the return path, unless that path is the deleted address's own pages, in which case they go to the address book list.
Posting a delete for an id that is not in the address book changes nothing, shows no banner and redirects as a delete would.
The source gives the delete action no extra check, such as whether the address is in use on a notification.
claims.note: Looked at the POST delete handler and deleteAddressBookEntry; nothing considers notifications that use the address. The page's inset says existing notifications keep it (see the delete inset claim).

The addresses offered at a postcode are the registered office addresses of live companies on the Companies House register, read from generated fixture files, one per postcode district (outward code).
claims.quote:
// Spike: registered office addresses for a postcode, from the Companies House
// files that `npm run build:postcode-addresses` writes.
claims.note: A prototype fixture source, not a real address lookup service. Address search is parked by programme ruling until the INS address lookup is real.

claims.statement: A postcode with no fixture file, or with no entry in its district's file, finds no addresses, so the select page shows "No addresses found for <postcode>".
claims.note: mechanism: reading the district fixture file. Follows from readPostcode returning [] and the select page's addressCount being 0.

claims.statement: Each found address has an id naming its postcode and its place in that postcode's list, such as ch-BB44JG-2, so the address form can find the address again from the id alone.
claims.quote:
// The id names the postcode and the address's place in that postcode's list
// (ch-BB44JG-2), so the forms can find the address again from the id alone.
claims.note: mechanism: id scheme for fixture addresses; the prototype's own way to pass a choice between pages.

claims.statement: A chosen address fills the address form by splitting its text at commas: the first part is address line 1, the last part (when there are two or more) is the town or city, and any parts between are address line 2; the name or organisation and county are left blank, the postcode is the formatted postcode and the country is United Kingdom.
claims.quote:
// "UNIT 1, YORK AVENUE, HASLINGDEN" becomes line 1 "UNIT 1", line 2
// "YORK AVENUE" and town "HASLINGDEN". A single part is line 1 only.
claims.note: mechanism: reshapes a one-line Companies House address into the address form's fields.

claims.statement: A UK address form lists the other addresses at the postcode where the user found the chosen address; when the address was not found by postcode, it lists the prototype's example UK addresses instead.
claims.quote:
// The addresses a UK address form lists: those at the postcode the user found
// the chosen address at, or the example addresses when there is none.
claims.note: mechanism: picks the address list an add-address form offers. The example addresses are address-book-lookup-addresses filtered to country 'United Kingdom'. The forms themselves belong to parts 8 and 16.

claims.statement: The prototype has a spike page at /postcode-lookup, headed and titled "Find an address by postcode", that is not linked into a journey and shows a "Spike" phase banner reading "Addresses come from the Companies House register of live companies."
claims.note: Not linked from a journey is inferred: nothing in this part's files links to /postcode-lookup, and it has no back link. The form posts to the unprefixed /postcode-lookup even under /design-release-2.1.

claims.statement: The spike page's form is submitted by GET and has one width-10 field labelled "Postcode" with the hint "A full UK postcode, like BB4 4AA" and a "Find address" button.

On the spike page an empty postcode shows "Enter a postcode" and a postcode that is not full shows "Enter a full UK postcode, like BB4 4AA", in a "There is a problem" summary linking to the field and beside the field, with "Error: " in the title.
When the spike page finds addresses it shows a "Registered office addresses" heading, the line "<N> address(es) found for <postcode>" and a bulleted list of each address followed by the postcode.
When the spike page finds no addresses it shows the heading "No registered office addresses found for <postcode>" and the line "Check the postcode, or try another one."
claims.quote:
No registered office addresses found for {{ lookup.postcode }}

Check the postcode, or try another one.

claims.statement: The spike page fails with an error, rather than reporting no addresses, when the postcode address files have not been built at all.
claims.quote: throw new Error(`No postcode address files in ${dir}: run npm run build:postcode-addresses`)
claims.note: mechanism: guards against a missing build of the fixture files. The find-address journey pages do not have this guard and show no addresses instead.
